Increasing Hund coupling suppresses the orbital response while increasing its spin polarization. Renormalized one-particle propagation alone does not reproduce this strong polarization dependence. These results extend compressed multiloop calculations to dynamical correlations in multiorbital environments.

items.title: Hybridization-Induced Enhancement of the Thermoelectric Response in the Kagome Material CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$
authors: Hongye Zhang, Boqin Song, Aifeng Wang, Yisheng Chai, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Ying Zhu, Tianping Ying, Mingquan He
items.summary: Flat bands in kagome lattices provide a prominent route to strongly correlated electronic states. Here we report charge and thermal transport measurements on single crystals of CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$, a kagome Kondo system arising from the hybridization between flat and dispersive bands. The Seebeck coefficient and Nernst signal increase rapidly below $T_\mathrm{F}\sim70$ K, concomitant with the emergence of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations and flat-band resonance. The Nernst coefficient in the intermediate-temperature range of $\sim30-80$ K further follows the universal scaling reported for prototypical heavy-fermion compounds, consistent with the development of strongly renormalized quasiparticles associated with hybridization. Both the Seebeck and Nernst responses reach extrema at a lower temperature $T_\mathrm{p}\sim20-25$ K, where phonon drag and correlated quasiparticles may both contribute. These results reveal a hybridization-induced enhancement of the thermoelectric response and establish CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$ as a kagome platform for probing flat-band-derived Kondo physics through thermoelectric transport.

items.title: First-principles modeling of ordering in Fe-rich Fe-Si alloys
authors: Daniil M. Khodachenko, Andrei V. Ruban, Franco Moitzi, Oleg E. Peil, Vsevolod I. Razumovskiy
items.summary: The atomic ordering in Fe-rich Fe-Si alloys strongly influences their magnetic properties and mechanical behavior. While general features of long-range atomic ordering are known from the experimentally established phase diagram in this composition range, detailed atomic configurations and driving forces behind them remain speculative. Here, we address this gap by using effective cluster interactions (ECI) obtained from density functional theory (DFT) calculations and subsequent statistical thermodynamics modeling to unravel the interplay between magnetism, composition, and temperature in body-centered cubic (bcc) Fe-Si alloys up to 20 at% Si. Our analysis reveals that the ordering behavior is governed by a strong coupling between magnetic order, lattice expansion, and Si concentration, with specific ECI shells switching sign or magnitude as the magnetic state changes, which is reflected in the phase equilibria and ordering behavior of Fe-Si alloys. In particular, we demonstrate that D0$_3$ ordering is, in fact, primary in the totally ordered ferromagnetic state, while the B2 type of ordering is promoted in the paramagnetic state at elevated temperatures. The temperature-dependent evolution of these ordering patterns, obtained from Monte Carlo simulations based on the magnetically resolved ECIs, reproduces the experimentally observed phase equilibria and short-range order characteristics. By explicitly linking the magnetic state with the effective interactions and macroscopic phase behavior, this work establishes a predictive framework for an ab initio-based description of ordering in Fe-rich Fe-Si alloys and highlights the decisive role of magnetism in ordering phenomena in this system.

items.title: Tuning Thermal Memory and Dissipation in Colloidal Glasses via Microgel Particle Stiffness
items.summary: The Kovacs effect, characterized by nonlinear, path-dependent structural recovery, is a hallmark of glassy systems. In soft colloidal microgel glasses, the stiffness of the constituent particles governs their deformation, swelling, rearrangement, and response to external stimuli, thereby dictating the path-dependent structural recovery of these jammed non-equilibrium systems. To investigate this influence, microgels of different stiffnesses were synthesized by adjusting the concentration of the polar crosslinker, N, N'-methylenebisacrylamide (MBA). The relaxation of the storage and loss moduli was measured using oscillatory rheology under diverse temperature ramp rates, and cryo-FESEM imaging provided direct visualization of the underlying particle packing. While the rapid adaptability of soft particles and the kinetic arrest of stiff ones suppresses Kovacs asymmetry, intermediate-stiffness particles exhibit moderate thermoresponsivity, traversing distinct energy landscapes on heating and cooling to maximize asymmetry and dissipation. Cryo-FESEM micrographs, displaying gel-like networks in soft particle suspensions, dense packing in stiff particle suspensions, and disordered, compact structures in intermediate-stiffness systems, corroborate these findings. Our results demonstrate that intermediate-stiffness PNIPAM microgels optimize structural recovery, rendering them promising candidates for forming colloidal glasses and establishing Kovacs asymmetry as a robust probe of non-equilibrium dynamics in glassy systems.

items.title: Super-tetragonal ferroelectric barium titanate through anionic overstoichiometry
authors: Jingtian Zhao, Johanna van Gent Gonz\'{a}lez, I\~nigo Robredo-Magro, Ewout van der Veer, Daniel A. Chaney, Jorge \'I\~niguez-Gonz\'alez, Beatriz Noheda, Martin F. Sarott
items.summary: Ferroelectric oxides, characterized by an electrical polarization that is switchable with an electric field, are an appealing class of materials for energy-efficient computing, electronics, and photonics. In thin films, the properties of ferroelectrics are commonly tuned using substrate-imposed epitaxial strain, an approach limited to biaxial strain states and a finite number of available substrates. Here, we demonstrate that is is possible to move beyond conventional epitaxial growth by using pulsed laser deposition under highly non-equilibrium conditions. Specifically, we show that this unconventional processing route allows us to stabilize a super-tetragonal phase of ferroelectric $\text{BaTiO}_3$. The key to this stabilization lies in the insertion of surplus oxygen atoms into the unit cell, resulting in peroxide bond formation that give rise to an aspect ratio of as high as 1.08. Notably, this super-tetragonal phase exhibits an enhanced ferroelectric polarization, reduced coercivity, lower leakage currents, and increased cycling endurance compared to conventional bulk-like $\text{BaTiO}_3$ films. These results, thus, showcase the potential of non-equilibrium growth for defect engineering to obtain emergent phases in complex oxides and tune their physical properties in thin films expanding the scope of traditional epitaxy.

items.title: Microscopic origin of field-induced multiferroicity in Ni3TeO6
authors: J. Lass, R. Toft-Petersen, A. A. Turrini, {\O}. S. Fjellv{\aa}g, B. Decrausaz, K. M. L. Krighaar, R. Sibille, H. Jacobsen, M. E. Kamminga, C. R. Y. Andersen, D. Sheptyakov, J. Ollivier, U. B. Hansen, M. Enderle, A. M. L\"auchli, H. M. R{\o}nnow, K. Lefmann, D. G. Mazzone
items.summary: The continued demand for smaller, faster, and more energy-efficient technologies has driven condensed-matter research towards materials combining multiple responses within a single phase. Particularly interesting examples are multiferroic materials featuring cross-couplings between order parameters. Ni3TeO6 is a prominent member of this material class, exhibiting a hysteresis-free transition under magnetic field which simultaneously affects the magnetic structure, electric polarization, and phonon frequencies. Here, we uncover the microscopic origin of this multiferroic transition using a combination of neutron scattering techniques. We establish the presence of a finite Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya exchange term giving rise to non-reciprocal, chiral spin waves which soften in magnetic field. Their condensation alters the magnetic structure which controls the electric polarization and drives an ionic displacement, thereby coupling the magnetic, electric, and lattice degrees of freedom. Our study demonstrates that neutron scattering is a powerful technique to elucidate microscopic interactions in multiferroic materials, informing the design of next-generation electronic devices.

items.title: Two-dimensional structures formed by pair potentials: An analytical and numerical study
items.summary: Understanding the thickness dependence of the excess energy of thin films and identifying the deviation from the scaling law that holds for thicker films are crucial for predicting the formation of two-dimensional (2D) materials derived from nonlayered structures, commonly referred to as non-van der Waals (non-vdW) 2D materials. Here, we analytically study the excess energy of thin films as a function of the number of layers $N$, assuming pair potentials. We show that the $1/N$ scaling law of the excess energy breaks down in the monolayer limit when the interatomic interactions are long-ranged. The analytical results are confirmed by numerical simulations using the Lennard-Jones and Morse potentials. The present work suggests that non-vdW 2D structures can be formed by pair potentials alone.

items.title: From hard-core to soft-core bosons in a shell trap
authors: G. Costa, S. Prestipino, F. Cinti, M. Ciardi
items.summary: We study the low-temperature states of a system of spinless bosons trapped in a broad spherical shell. In our virtual (path-integral Monte Carlo) experiments, we specifically examine how the equilibrium structure and overall superfluidity of the system are affected by a change of the interparticle-potential core from hard to increasingly soft. In this manner we bridge the gap between the behaviors of two species of bosons: Helium-like atoms, which self-assemble into ordinary crystalline solids, and Rydberg-dressed atoms, which in simulation form cluster (super)solids. We also vary the particle mass, i.e., the quantumness of the system, so as to modify the relative stability of ``solid'' and fluid states. We thus find a whole spectrum of (finite-size) phases with a curved structure, including multilayer and cluster phases, as well as superfluids and single layer supersolids. In particular, we confirm that supersolids only occur in the presence of clusters. By considering three system sizes (from 60 to 180 particles), but rescaling the trap radius so that the density stays fixed, we verify that supersolid states only exist in the same range of particle masses. Our model serves as a platform to test how emergent properties are modified, in spherical geometry, in the crossover from atoms to dressed atoms.

items.title: Suppressing Majorana Hybridization in Atomically Assembled Cr Chains on Bi2Pd
authors: Jinkyung Kim, Piotr Kot, Ryo Ogawa, Atustaka Maeda, Andreas J. Heinrich, Nicolas Lorente, Deung-Jang Choi
items.summary: Magnetic-atom chains on superconductors can host Majorana zero modes, but in finite chains the two end modes generally hibridize and split away from zero energy. We show that Cr chains assembled atom-by-atom on the Bi-terminated surface of Bi2Pd enter a short-localization-length Shiba chain regime wthat strongly suppreesses this finite-size hybridization. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals a chaing-leght-driven closing and reopening of the in-gap spectrum, followed by zero-bias modes localized at the chains ends. Green-function calculations reproduce the evolution and show an exchange of electorn-holec haracter across the transition. From the residual splitting we extract a localization length of about three atomic sites, explaining the stability of the zero-energy modes in experimentally accessible chains.

items.title: Room-temperature near-infrared optical readout of triplet spin states integrated in carbon nanotubes towards quantum sensing
authors: J. Alejandro de Sousa, Ilias Vandevenne, Jana Nikoli\'c, Tuur Boonen, Etienne Goovaerts, Sofie Cambr\'e
items.summary: Optically addressable electron spin qubits that function at room temperature and under ambient conditions are essential for advancing quantum sensing. Solid state defect platforms offer robust spin-photon interfaces but lack precise defect positioning and electronic tunability. Molecular spin qubits enable bottom up chemical design yet suffer from limited photostability. Here, we introduce para-halophenyl (-Cl, -Br and -I) quantum defects in (6,5) single wall carbon nanotubes that trap triplet excitons with a spin-photon interface that is operable under ambient, room temperature conditions. These defects were shown to emit in the near infrared within the biological transparency window, and their placement on the nanotube surface provides nanoscale proximity to target environments. The deep optical traps formed by the defects yield exceptional photostability. Here, we demonstrate optical initialization and readout of these triplet states at room temperature, provide proof of principle sensing of paramagnetic molecules, and highlight potential for on chip detection. Together, these results establish SWCNT defects as a promising new platform for future quantum sensing.

items.title: Chiral-Nematic Lattice Instability in Charge Density Wave of 1T-TiSe2
authors: Abdurrafi Ahsan Alghifari, Euihwan Do, Jae Whan Park, Han Woong Yeom
items.summary: Chiral charge-density waves (CDWs) are a rare form of electronic order with handedness, enabling novel couplings among light, lattice, and topology in quantum materials. Yet the microscopic origin of chirality has remained elusive, even in the prototypical chiral CDW system 1T-TiSe2. Using ab initio calculations, we investigate the structural stability and electronic structure of competing CDW models in 1T-TiSe2. We show that a chiral monoclinic (C2) structure is stabilized by the cooperative condensation of multiple phonon modes and reproduces the chiral topography and energy gap observed experimentally. We further find an exceptionally soft potential landscape around this energy-minimized structure, along the direction that removes the remaining rotational symmetry, allowing the lattice to fluctuate through fully asymmetric configurations while its average structure remains chiral. This dynamical chiral CDWnaturally reconciles the chiral domains seen by time-averaged topographic probes with the complete loss of symmetry detected by bulk spectroscopy, and clarifies how chiral CDWs emerge from the interplay of lattice instability and fluctuation.

items.title: Higher-order Angular Momentum Transport of Alteraxial Phonons in 2D Magnets
authors: Linxin Liu, Fuyi Wang, Huaiqiang Wang
items.summary: The coupling between lattice vibrations and magnetic order in two-dimensional (2D) magnets gives rise to a variety of physical phenomena, among which magnetic effects of axial phonons carrying phonon angular momentum (PAM) have attracted considerable interest. However, a systematic classification of axial phonons in 2D magnets that covers their multipolar patterns and the resulting transport manifestations remains largely unexplored. Here, based on symmetry analysis, we classify all 2D magnetic point groups by their long-wavelength PAM wave patterns. Beyond the s-wave axial phonon, we identify alteraxial phonons with p-, d-, f-, g-, and i-wave multipolar textures, characterized by 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 zero-PAM nodal lines, respectively. We then develop a theory of nonlinear PAM transport driven by a temperature gradient and derive two selection rules: a parity selection rule that determines whether the response occurs at even or odd orders, and an angular-harmonic selection rule that fixes the lowest allowed order for each wave pattern. The multipolar PAM patterns and selection rules are exemplified by two effective lattice models realizing f-wave and d-wave PAM patterns, respectivley. The angular dependence of the nonlinear PAM current reflects the underlying multipolar PAM texture, offering a signature for experiments. Our results establish a symmetry-guided framework for detecting and utilizing higher-order PAM textures in 2D magnets.

items.title: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4
authors: Keita Nagasawa, Ryutaro Okuma, Jun-ichi Yamaura, Yoshihiko Okamoto
items.summary: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) usually relies on magnetic ordering, which fixes a preferred moment orientation and couples it to charge transport. Here, we demonstrate that pronounced AMR can instead arise from the anisotropic magnetic-field-induced polarization of dilute local moments in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4, a quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals narrow-gap semiconductor. Magnetization measurements reveal Curie-like paramagnetism down to 2 K, with the c axis as the magnetic easy axis. The magnetization is described by an effective S = 1/2 model with an anisotropic g-factor ratio of g_c/g_ab = 1.43(1). With the electrical current applied along the c axis, the Fe-doped sample exhibits a large negative magnetoresistance for B//c and only a weak positive response for B//ab, whereas the undoped sample shows little magnetoresistance for either field orientation. The resulting AMR ratio reaches -33% at 8 K and 10 T and exhibits a nonmonotonic temperature dependence qualitatively captured by a minimal spin-disorder model. These results show that engineering the local environment of dilute magnetic ions provides a route to large paramagnetic AMR without long-range magnetic order, extending the materials design space for AMR beyond magnetically ordered systems.

items.title: On thermal Hall effect in boson systems
authors: Yu. V. Baramygina, D. N. Aristov
items.summary: We theoretically discuss the thermal Hall effect (THE) in boson systems keeping in mind possible applications to magnetically ordered insulators with skyrmion lattice ground state. The magnon spectrum of such systems may undergo a topological transition upon the variation of magnetic field, and THE could be a tool to confirm this phenomenon. We rederive formulas, suitable for our purposes, and find expressions which have a different temperature dependence of THE as compared to previously reported results. Particularly, in presence of anomalous terms in magnon Hamiltonian the thermal Hall conductivity has a small but finite residual 1/T contribution. Such contribution may become sizable at very low temperatures and resembles Meissner effect in superconducting metals.

items.title: Quantum Interference Enhanced Rectification in Mesoscopic Nanowires
authors: T. J. Osborne, B. Braunecker, H. F. Legg
items.summary: Nanoscale nonreciprocal elements are needed to control signal flow in scalable quantum technologies, but existing nonreciprocal components are often bulky. Here, we show that a strongly nonreciprocal current-voltage relation can arise entirely from coherent elastic scattering in a mesoscopic Rashba nanowire with gate-defined scatterers. We first identify the symmetry constraints that enforce reciprocal transmission in a phase coherent conductor even when inversion and time-reversal symmetry are broken. We then show how gates that are capacitively coupled to the leads, together with a magnetic scatterer or transverse subband mixing, can remove these constraints. In the weak-scattering regime, nonreciprocal conductance originates from interference between distinct backscattering paths. In the strong-scattering regime, nonreciprocity can be resonantly enhanced by the hybridization of the transmitting channel with bound states that arise from a higher transverse subband or spin-split band. In this regime, we find that a bias-induced change in the gate potentials of about one percent can produce an order-unity diode response, i.e., electrons are transmitted almost as in a clean wire for one bias polarity, whereas for the other polarity the current is strongly suppressed.

items.title: Interaction-Induced Bloch Geometry and Transverse Thermoelectric Transport
authors: Heng-Yu Di, YuanDong Wang, Zhen-Gang Zhu, Gang Su
items.summary: Electron--electron interactions can reconstruct Bloch wave functions, changing their geometry and the associated thermoelectric response. We derive the linear thermoelectric response within the Hartree--Fock (HF) approximation using the thermal length-gauge density-matrix approach, resolving Drude, symmetric quantum-metric, and antisymmetric Berry-curvature contributions. In a noninteracting Bloch eigenbasis, we separate the reconstructed Berry connection into the noninteracting connection and an interaction connection. This gives bare, coherence, and interaction-connection contributions to the anomalous thermoelectric response. We determine the constraints imposed by spatial inversion, rotational, time-reversal, and combined symmetries on the three transport channels. In the relaxation-time approximation, the leading weak-broadening behavior is $\Gamma^{-1}$ for the Drude contribution, $\Gamma$ for the quantum-metric contribution, and $\Gamma^0$ for the Berry-curvature contribution. The interband scalings apply away from band degeneracies. Self-consistent calculations for the triangular-lattice extended Hubbard model illustrate how interactions generate Berry curvature and a quantum metric, change the symmetry of the system, and thereby contribute to transverse thermoelectric transport.

items.title: Splitting Probability in Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Prashant Singh, Sabine Tornow, David A Kessler, Eli Barkai
items.summary: We consider a continuous-time quantum walk stroboscopically subjected to projective measurements on two distinct targets with sampling time period $\tau$. We construct a general renewal framework for the first-detection amplitude at each target, from which we obtain the associated splitting probabilities. For Hamiltonians with reflection symmetry, we further show that each dual-target first-detection amplitude can be viewed as an interference effect between a pair of single-target first-detection amplitudes. This formulation yields exact expressions for the splitting probabilities and gives special sampling times at which they undergo pointwise discontinuous jumps due to a form of ergodicity breaking associated with dark states. As an illustrative example, we apply the framework to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice chain with nearest-neighbor hopping, and study the splitting probabilities as functions of the initial position and sampling time. Below a critical sampling time, $0<\tau < \tau_c$ where $\tau_c = 2 \pi / \Delta E$ with $\Delta E$ being the energy bandwidth, the splitting probabilities for large system sizes become equal to $1/2$, independent of the initial position, as long as this position does not coincide with target sites. Above the critical sampling time, $\tau \geq \tau_c$, the splitting probabilities deviate from $1/2$ and develop oscillations as a function of initial position. The wavenumber associated with these oscillations is $Q=2\sin^{-1}(r\tau_c/\tau)$, where $r$ is a positive integer. We also explore the effects of relative phase and spatial separation between different components of a coherent initial state on the splitting probabilities. Finally, we study how a finite number of measurements modifies the splitting probabilities and broadens the resonances at special sampling times.

items.title: Superconductivity via repulsive interaction in the model with electrons and holes
items.summary: We study a toy model of the 2D electron gas including electron-like and hole-like charge carriers hybridized between each other. Electrons and holes can move either in different layers or in the same layer. Undoped system is an insulator. Slight doping brings extra charge carriers having large density of states. We show that the screened Coulomb interaction is enough to stabilize the superconductivity in the slightly doped system. The symmetry of the order parameter corresponds to the spin-triplet $p$-wave order. For realistic values of the model parameters the superconducting transition temperature can reach the value of $150$ kelvin.

items.title: Microstructural evolution during isothermal tempering of a highly supersaturated metastable austenitic state of a PM high-speed steel
authors: Stefan M\"uller, Santiago Benito, Hendric Schaefer, Yujiao Li, Leonhard Gertlowski, Oliver Schenk, Ulrich Hagemann, Christoph Broeckmann, Sebastian Weber
items.summary: This study investigates the microstructural evolution of the powder metallurgical high-speed steel PM HS 3-3-4 during isothermal holding within the transformation gap between pearlite and bainite formation. The focus is on the mechanism of carbide spheroidization and the proposed formation of a chemically graded carbide rim. The heat treatments were carried out in a quenching dilatometer, enabling precise control of the thermal cycles and isothermal holding conditions. Spatially resolved analytic microscopy techniques, including scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), Auger electron spectroscopy (AES) and atom probe tomography (APT), image analysis and complementary thermodynamic simulations (MatCalc) were used to characterize the carbide evolution. Isothermal holding increased carbide circularity, carbide volume fraction, and hardness, while MatCalc calculations predict a strong thermodynamic driving force for additional carbide precipitation. The analytic techniques revealed a compositional gradient of approximately 15 nm at the carbide-matrix interface in the isothermally treated condition, compared with a sharp transition of only 2-3 nm in the directly quenched state. This nanometer-scale gradient provides strong evidence for epitaxial, interface-controlled carbide growth and the formation of a chemically graded carbide rim. The associated solute depletion of the surrounding austenite provides a plausible explanation for its reduced stability, reflected by an increase in the martensite start temperature. The combined results demonstrate that isothermal holding promotes interfacial chemical reorganization, offering new insights into carbide spheroidization and providing a basis for tailoring carbide morphology and the resulting mechanical properties through heat treatment.

items.title: Stochastic resonance in time-delayed bistable active particles
authors: Antonio A. Valido, Mattia Coccolo, Miguel A. F. Sanju\'an
items.summary: We investigate analytically and numerically stochastic resonance in an underdamped active (Ornstein--Uhlenbeck) particle confined in a bistable potential with time-delayed feedback and subjected to an additional (non-thermal) white-noise source. Restricting the analysis to the active-noise-dominated bistable regime, with sufficiently short delay and active-noise correlation times, we develop a perturbative theory that yields analytical expressions for both the escape rate and the spectral power amplification within the framework of linear-response theory, without invoking detailed balance. The analytical predictions are in qualitative agreement with direct numerical simulations throughout the perturbative regime. We show that a moderate increase in the active-noise correlation time can enhance the stochastic-resonance response, in marked contrast to previous results for overdamped passive systems driven by colored noise. Conversely, the addition of white noise weakens the resonant response and shifts its optimum toward lower active-noise intensities. Time-delayed feedback further alters the matching condition between the escape rate and the driving frequency while preserving the resonant mechanism. Beyond the perturbative regime, we find that finite-memory effects progressively broaden the resonance profile and substantially decrease its amplitude. Overall, these results provide new insight into the combined role of inertia, activity, environmental fluctuations, and time delayed feedback in stochastic resonance in nonequilibrium systems.

items.title: Perpendicular Magnetization from Crystallite Boundaries in Polycrystalline Antiferromagnetic $\gamma$-FeMn
authors: Rachel E. Maizel, Sachli Abdizadeh, Ali Almahmoud, Omolara A. Bakare, Galen T. Street, Hanu Arava, Sauviz P. Alaei, Sanyum Channa, Daisy A. O'Mahoney, Rishav Khatiwada, Jing Zhao, Charis Horn, Evan Stocker, Benjamin Kostroun, Emilio Corrales, Christoph Klewe, Alpha T. N'Diaye, Yuri Suzuki, Jean J. Heremans, Frederick M. Michel, Mitsuhiro Murayama, Vsevolod M. Ivanov, Satoru Emori
items.summary: Single-crystalline noncollinear antiferromagnets, such as Mn$_3$Sn, are actively explored as memory media, but they generally require high-temperature growth that is incompatible with industrial-scale device fabrication. Here, we show that polycrystalline films of antiferromagnetic $\gamma$-FeMn, grown at room temperature, develop a perpendicular magnetization and an anomalous Hall effect, opening an industrially compatible route to antiferromagnetic memory. While conventional noncollinear antiferromagnets demand near-perfect crystal order, $\gamma$-FeMn films derive their memory-enabling properties from crystal defects, particularly boundaries separating nanoscale crystallites. When the crystallite size $D$ falls below $\approx$ 30 nm, a field-switchable magnetization emerges and increases with the boundary density $\propto 1/D$. This magnetization is accompanied by a room-temperature anomalous Hall conductivity exceeding 10 S/cm, comparable to that of single-crystalline Mn$_3$Sn. Our systematic experimental results, including scanning magnetometry, indicate uncompensated spin moments in the boundaries coupled to the compensated antiferromagnetism within the crystallites. We further find that the perpendicular easy axis of the magnetization is stabilized by residual strain within the $\gamma$-FeMn film. Our findings in manufacturing-friendly polycrystalline $\gamma$-FeMn redefine crystal defects as enablers, rather than impediments, for scalable antiferromagnetic memory.

items.title: Mechanism of delayed elastic state absorption versus fatigue failure in cyclic shear of amorphous materials
authors: Samuel B. Walker, Suzanne M. Fielding
items.summary: We study cyclic shear in a lattice elastoplastic model of amorphous materials. The model displays a threshold shear amplitude $\gamma_{\rm c}$, which increases with sample annealing. For imposed amplitudes $\gamma_0\lesssim\gamma_{\rm c}$, it shows slow progression to an absorbing elastic state. For $\gamma_0\gtrsim \gamma_{\rm c}$, it shows slow fatigue and delayed material failure. Our key contribution is to elucidate a mechanistic understanding of this behaviour. We show that progression to an absorbing state maps to single element diffusion on a finite interval with two absorbing boundaries. We derive expressions for the decay rate of the fraction of active elements, and the survival distribution. The diffusing variable is the local elemental strain, which takes two jumps stroboscopically per cycle. Once the value at any site diffuses below its yielding threshold, the element behaves elastically. This leads to a gradual accumulation of strains just below threshold. For $\gamma_0\lesssim \gamma_{\rm c}$ this diffusive behaviour is preceded by many cycles in which cooperativity between elements via stress propagation is also important. For $\gamma_0 > \gamma_{\rm c}$, stress propagation dominates and precipitates failure. For $\gamma_0\gtrsim \gamma_{\rm c}$, the same accumulation of elements just below local threshold that led to an elastic state for $\gamma_0\lesssim\gamma_{\rm c}$ accounts for the fatigue that brings the system to the brink of failure. We evidence this via simulations in which the strain amplitude artificially exceeds $\gamma_0 $ in each half cycle, before reverting to the system's actual state at $\pm\gamma_0$ and resuming the next half cycle. During fatigue, the stress-strain slope $d\sigma/d\gamma$ evolves towards unity at $|\gamma|=\gamma_0^-$, signifying perfect elasticity within cycle, yet towards zero at $|\gamma|=\gamma_0^+$, precipitating failure.

items.title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity
authors: Rustam Arabov, Konstantin Sozykin, Nikita Rybin, Alexander Shapeev
items.summary: Accurate and efficient prediction of lattice thermal conductivity (LTC) is essential for developing materials for thermoelectric, microelectronic, and photovoltaic applications. Here, we present a methodology for high-throughput calculation of LTC across large datasets of compounds sharing a common crystal symmetry. Our approach combines fine-tuning of the MatterSim 1M universal machine-learned interatomic potential with LTC calculations based on the solution of the Boltzmann transport equation. We introduce a symmetry-based few-shot fine-tuning strategy (SBFS-FT) based on low-rank adaptation. In this approach, MatterSim 1M is fine-tuned on a small, carefully selected set of compounds that share a common crystal symmetry. The resulting potential is then applicable for accurate LTC calculations for compounds with this crystal symmetry, even if they were not included in the fine-tuning set. We tested our methodology on datasets of half-Heusler compounds (space group 216), materials with space group 225, and spinels (space group 227). We demonstrated that LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M fine-tuned using SBFS-FT exhibited a mean absolute relative difference from the reference results (obtained using moment tensor potentials and polyMLPs) 2-3 times smaller than that achieved with the non-fine-tuned MatterSim 1M potential. Moreover, the accuracy of LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M after SBFS-FT was comparable to that achieved using the MatterSim 1M potentials individually fine-tuned for each compound. Importantly, SBFS-FT enabled generation of the potential suitable for accurate LTC calculations across large compound datasets substantially faster than fine-tuning of MatterSim 1M for each compound individually, reducing the computational time by approximately a factor of 5-7 for a dataset of 100 compounds.

items.title: Confirmation of complex non-collinear Fe(II) spin ordering in the iron oxychalcogenide La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ by broad range $^{139}$La-NQR
authors: Tillmann Weinhold, Jerin Abraham George, Cornelius Herrmann, Domenic Nowak, Rajib Sarkar, Felix Seewald, Rowena Wachtel, Sabine Wurmehl, Bernd B\"uchner, Hans-Henning Klauss

items.title: Construction of highly coarse-grained molecular models for aqueous electrolytes
authors: Michael A. Seaton, Benjamin T. Speake, Tristan Rimmer, Ilian T. Todorov
items.summary: Molecular modelling of electrochemical systems at larger than atomic scales poses particular challenges, not least the ability to represent correct thermodynamic, hydrodynamic and dielectric properties while still being computationally viable for large scale applications. In the case of aqueous electrolytes such as those used in vanadium-based batteries with oxidation-reduction (redox) reactions, both a background medium that can respond to localised electric fields due to high-valence ions and control over ion transport properties are crucial to embed consistently in the model. To this end, we propose the use of Dissipative Particle Dynamics (DPD) combined with a newly-devised highly coarse-grained polarisable water model with pairwise interactions designed to produce realistic thermodynamic behaviour as the basis for the aqueous electrolytes found in vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFB). We consider how the core water model can be modified to incorporate the ionic species found in VRFB catholytes and anolytes, as well as how the DPD pairwise thermostat forces can be parameterised to attain realistic diffusivities for those species.

items.title: Energy-fed commitment: a minimal model of random selection followed by reinforcement
items.summary: When a symmetric instability is crossed, fluctuations choose one of several equivalent branches. We study a minimal stochastic model of what can then make that choice progressively harder to undo. After selection, the stiffness of the selected state grows in proportion to the energy released each time the structure recovers from a perturbation; in this conservative model that energy equals, up to small and explicitly computed terms, the work absorbed from the perturbing agent. The model is a phenomenological closure with one coupling constant. That energy reinforces a branch already chosen, rather than choosing it, is an assumption of the model, which we state and do not derive. Its consequences are quantitative. The growth of commitment depends on how the structure is driven: geometric under displacement control, linear under energy control and sublinear under force control, so that committed states absorb more work per cycle under displacement control and less under force control. Reinforcement suppresses reversal exponentially; beyond a finite commitment the alternative minimum disappears and reversals become rare crossings of an irreversibility threshold. With unbounded reinforcement a choice is retained forever with positive probability under stated conditions; with saturating reinforcement retention is finite, with a lifetime that grows exponentially with the saturation level. Exact first-passage calculations agree with stochastic simulations; these verify the closure and its analysis but cannot test the physical postulate. We identify the experiments that could: protocols that separate absorbed energy from the number of perturbations, and driven steady states with nonzero housekeeping heat, in which heat and absorbed work differ.

items.title: Zero-group-velocity modes in textured steel plates: experiments and elastic modeling
authors: C. Gr\"unsteidl, C. Kerschbaummayr, G. Yan, G. Watzl, F. Rudinger, E. Scherleitner, M. Sonnleitner, C. Hoflehner
items.summary: Zero-group-velocity (ZGV) resonances are investigated as a non-contact ultrasonic probe of elastic anisotropy in textured steel plates. Directional laser-ultrasonic measurements were performed on 70% cold-rolled Ti-stabilized interstitial-free steel plates in the full-hard and recrystallized condition. Experimental results were compared with predictions based on effective elastic stiffness tensors derived from X-ray diffraction measurements. Classical Voigt-Reuss-Hill estimates and microstructure-resolved finite-element homogenization reproduce the measured angular dependence of the ZGV frequencies well for both states, with the finite-element KUBC/SUBC bounds considerably narrower than the classical Voigt-Reuss bounds. For the full-hard state, agreement with the texture-based model is obtained only after a recovery treatment. This indicates that dislocations present in the full-hard material contribute to its elastic response, an interpretation that is further supported by theoretical estimations. An identifiability analysis shows that the directional ZGV measurements provide access to at least three independently observable combinations of the stiffness tensor components, and concluding suggestions for application in recrystallization monitoring are provided.

items.title: Effect of Annealing on Maze Domains in Topological Insulator - Magnetic Multilayer Heterostructures
authors: Benjamin A. Brereton, Soumyarup Hait, Christy J. Kinane, Francesco Maccherozzi, Ahmet Yagmur, Satoshi Sasaki, Thomas A. Moore, Sean Langridge, Christopher H. Marrows
items.summary: Combining topological insulators with chiral magnetic multilayers offers the opportunity to greatly enhance the spin-orbit torque (SOT) driven manipulation of hosted spin textures, however this also exposes devices to the often poor temperature stability of the commonly used, Bi$_2$X$_3$-based (X is a chalcogenic element), topological insulator films. In this work we demonstrate through in-situ-annealing and polarised neutron reflectometry that the multilayer at a Bi$_2$Se$_3$ interface remains magnetically robust up to a temperature of 350 $^{\circ}$C: even as the Bi$_2$Se$_3$ epilayer structurally deteriorates. Through x-ray photoemission electron microscopy, an intermediate annealing temperature of $\sim$ 200 $^{\circ}$C was found to improve the domain ordering of the multilayer, allowing for field-induced skyrmion nucleation, all whilst sustaining minimal damage to the topological insulator

items.title: Hydrodynamics of microalgae in sea spray
authors: Elettra Fig\`a Talamanca, Juliette Pierre, Eva Ternon, Paula Cohen, Maarten De Rijcke, H\'el\`ene de Maleprade
items.summary: Airborne transmission of biological matter is likely to cause numerous respiratory distress in coastal populations during certain harmful algal blooms. While we know that dissolved algal toxins aerosolize, the contribution of particle-associated toxins is still unknown. The observation of microalgae in the atmosphere suggests that cells or cell debris could be a carrier. Exchange of particulate matter between ocean and atmosphere is driven by sea spray: microplastics and bacteria aerosolize in jet droplets, following the bursting of air bubbles. However, current models for particle capture only consider surface effects, which fail to explain how large microalgal cells (5-50 um) can be entrapped in jet drops (100-800 um). Here, we demonstrate with a variety of species that microalgae are consistently captured in jet drops, and derive a new particle capture model based on the hydrodynamics of the jet. Using the enrichment factor, which measures the increase in concentration in the first jet drop relative to the bulk, we uncover two regimes. The transition between regimes strongly depends on cell size. In addition, we highlight the dynamics of particles within the jet and derive an enrichment model based on hydrodynamics rather than surface considerations. This work widens and generalizes established results on bacterial and microplastic entrapment in jet drops, resolving discrepancies found in the literature. Finally, we demonstrate that sea spray can aerosolize toxic Ostreopsis cf. ovata cells. This reveals a potential particulate pathway for airborne toxicity during harmful algal blooms and raises the question of the relative contribution of particles to that of dissolved toxins.

items.title: Electric-field tunable spin texture in dual-gated HfS$_2$/graphene van der Waals heterostructures
authors: Haozhe Yang, Zhendong Chi, Eoin Dolan, Josep Ingla-Ayn\'es, Beatriz Mart\'in-Garc\'ia, Witold Skowro\'nski, Marco Gobbi, Andrey Chuvilin, Luis E. Hueso, F\`elix Casanova
items.summary: Spin-charge interconversion provides the essential link between spin information and electrical signals in spintronic devices. In spin-orbit coupled systems, spin-charge interconversion can contain multiple components associated with different spin-polarization directions, reflecting the underlying spin texture. Tuning this spin texture therefore provides a way to control not only the magnitude of spin-charge interconversion, but also the balance among its different components. Graphene-based van der Waals heterostructures provide an attractive platform for this purpose because interfacial spin-orbit coupling can host multiple spin-charge interconversion channels that couple to different spin-polarization directions. Here, we demonstrate electric-field control of spin texture in a dual-gated HfS$_2$/graphene van der Waals heterostructure, where independent control of carrier density and vertical electric field allows us to disentangle electrostatic doping from electric field-induced spin-orbit effects. Nonlocal spin precession measurements show that near zero vertical electric field, spin-charge interconversion is dominated by a spin Hall component with out-of-plane spins. Increasing the vertical electric field enhances additional in-plane spin components with Rashba-Edelstein-like character, including both parallel and perpendicular to the charge current contributions. These results provide experimental evidence that a vertical electric field can reconfigure the effective spin texture and control the corresponding spin-charge interconversion components, demonstrating electrical tunability of spin-orbit functionalities.

items.title: Quantum criticality in a two-component two-dimensional nematic metal
items.summary: Nematic fluctuations alter the low-energy electronic behavior and reshape the mean-field phase diagram. We study a two-dimensional nematic metal with a two-component internal degree of freedom. Near the quantum critical point (QCP), longitudinal nematic fluctuations generate the non-Fermi-liquid self-energy $\propto|\omega|^{2/3}$, whereas transverse fluctuations give a subleading logarithmic, marginal-Fermi-liquid correction. Nevertheless, the transverse sector dominates the correction to the phase diagram through a quantum order-by-disorder mechanism: the emergent nematic background reshapes the electronic spectrum, alters the decay of nematic bosons, and produces a negative singular free-energy correction. This correction reconstructs the phase diagram, drives the transition first order, and is described by a scaling function whose two asymptotic limits define two critical regimes with free-energy corrections scaling as $R^{8/3}$ and $R^3$, respectively, where $R$ is the order-parameter magnitude; their powers follow from the competition between the characteristic momentum of normal-state nematic fluctuations and that of the ordered-state background. These two regimes are experimentally distinguishable through nematic-susceptibility hysteresis measurements. The corrected phase diagram shows that the enlarged nodal $\alpha$ phase masks the otherwise bare QCP, making it inaccessible; consequently, the logarithmic self-energy correction is by no means negligible at low energies.

items.title: Microscopic Parametric Correlations and Spectral Rigidity in the Non-Hermitian Threefold Way
items.summary: We study microscopic spectral correlations between two nearby parameter values in the three non-Hermitian Gaussian bulk classes: $A$ (unconstrained), $AI^\dagger$ (complex symmetric), and $AII^\dagger$ (complex self-dual, with each degenerate doublet counted once). Parameter dependence is modelled by stationary matrix Ornstein--Uhlenbeck evolution, whose microscopic time scale is $N^{-1}$. For every positive integer replica number $n$, we derive exact finite-$N$ auxiliary-field integral representations for joint characteristic-polynomial moments and obtain their bulk asymptotics as $N\to\infty$ with $n$ fixed. With the spectrum normalized to the unit disk, correlations near a bulk point $z_0$, between spectral positions $z_1,z_2$ at times $t_1,t_2$, depend only on $s=N|z_1-z_2|^2+N(1-|z_0|^2)|t_1-t_2|$. Adopting the static Hermitian/non-Hermitian replica continuation yields explicit two-time kernels; for $AI^\dagger$ and $AII^\dagger$ these are replica conjectures and, to our knowledge, the first microscopic two-time kernels proposed for these classes. They determine density correlations, cross-time eigenvalue-count covariances, and equal-time number variances. For a disk of mean eigenvalue count $y$, the latter obey $\mbox{Var}\mathcal N_X(D_y)=\kappa_X\sqrt y+ \beta_X/\sqrt y+o(y^{-1/2})$, with explicitly given constants for each class. Exact perturbation theory further identifies eigenvector nonorthogonality as the mechanism of short-time spectral diffusion and yields a basis-independent condition number for a two-dimensional Kramers eigenspace in class $AII^\dagger$. Direct simulations agree quantitatively with its conjectured inverse-gamma law.

items.title: An Instability of the Quantum Markov Length
items.summary: The Markov length, the length scale governing the exponential decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) in a quantum many-body state, has proven useful for characterizing mixed-state phases of matter. Nevertheless, we show that a state's Markov length is not generally stable under weak local channels. The failure of stability occurs already at a pure product state. We demonstrate this explicitly in a one-dimensional fermionic chain, where a fine-tuned depth-two circuit of nearest-neighbor Gaussian channels maps the vacuum to a state whose CMI decays \emph{algebraically} and whose Markov length is therefore infinite, even when the channels are taken arbitrarily close to the identity. The algebraic decay is rooted in the nonanalyticity of the von Neumann entropy at rank-deficient density operators. We exhibit an analogous instability on an ordinary qubit chain. More generally, we show that the Markov length is unstable in any translation-invariant state with even a single rank-deficient reduced density operator. These results pose a challenge to recent definitions of mixed-state phase equivalence based on the Markov length.

items.title: Liouvillian Non-Invertible Symmetry
authors: Ying-Cheng Yang, Jhen-Dong Lin, Yueh-Nan Chen
items.summary: Non-invertible symmetries extend conventional symmetries beyond group-like transformations and play an important role in quantum field theory and many-body physics. However, a general framework of non-invertible symmetries in open quantum systems is still lacking. Here, we formulate a general Liouville-space duality framework that extends Hilbert-space non-invertible dualities to open quantum systems. The resulting defect relates Liouvillians with dual Hamiltonian and dissipative parameters and becomes an exact symmetry at self-duality. We apply this framework to the periodic transverse-field Ising chain with two collective Lindblad channels exchanged by Kramers--Wannier (KW) duality. A strong $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry divides Liouville space into four parity sectors, while the defect acts nontrivially only in the even-even sector. At self-duality, the KW defect imposes a momentum-resolved selection rule on Liouvillian Jordan blocks. Modes with different Liouville momenta or KW-defect eigenvalues cannot form a common exceptional Jordan block. For a three-site chain, a global R\'enyi-2 KW asymmetry dynamically identifies the self-dual conditions. At the same time, the spectral structure exhibits both a semisimple degeneracy and a self-dual exceptional point with a perturbation-selective response. These results extend non-invertible dualities to Markovian quantum dynamics and establish a symmetry-based selection rule for Liouvillian Jordan structures.

items.title: Spectral signatures of hidden order and hidden quantum critical points
authors: Reja H. Wilke, Henning Schl\"omer, Sebastian Paeckel, Annabelle Bohrdt, Fabian Grusdt
items.summary: Hidden-order phases elude the conventional Ginzburg-Landau framework: although they spontaneously break symmetry, their order remains invisible to standard local two-point correlators. Instead, they are typically characterized by nonlocal (string) order parameters and are believed to underlie a range of exotic quantum states, such as symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases. While hidden correlations have previously been detected through nonlocal observables in quantum gas microscope experiments, in realistic solid-state systems multipoint observables are typically inaccessible and the signatures of hidden order remain largely unexplored. In this work, we show that hidden order in doped spin chains can be directly probed through dynamical two-point response functions measurable by resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and neutron scattering. Focusing on a minimal model, we numerically identify clear spectral fingerprints of both the hidden-order phase, its associated hidden quantum critical point as well as a specific group of gapless SPT phases. Complementing our numerical results with analytical insights, we uncover the microscopic origin of these spectral signatures and demonstrate how they emerge from the interplay between spin and charge degrees of freedom. Together, our results establish spectroscopy as a practical probe of hidden order and gapless SPT phases and provide a unified understanding of the low-energy physics governing these unconventional quantum phases.

items.title: An Open-Source Data Infrastructure for Alloy Synthesis Research: Stage 1 --- Composition Screening and Literature Cross-Referencing
items.summary: Experimental materials-science labs routinely accumulate synthesis and characterization data across spreadsheets, instrument export files, and ad-hoc folders, with no durable link between a sample's recipe, its measured properties, and whether a similar composition has been reported elsewhere. We present Stage 1 of an open-source data infrastructure closing this loop for a single working alloy-synthesis lab: a relational schema for composition and synthesis records, a strict composition/mass calculator, three empirical alloy-design screening metrics (VEC, atomic-size mismatch, mixing enthalpy) plus a melt/boil-point synthesis-feasibility check, an automated cross-referencing layer against three public materials databases (Materials Project, OQMD, Alexandria) with deduplication and adjustable relevance filtering, and a desktop GUI unifying the workflow behind a single "new entry" action. Built and used by a practicing researcher rather than a software team, we report it as a systems/methodology contribution - the architecture, the concrete engineering failures encountered while building it, and how each was diagnosed and fixed - rather than new materials-science results. We argue the specific defects found - a parser ambiguity that produced silent wrong answers, a partial code edit that broke a dependency chain invisibly, a database-metadata bug traceable to an un-cast numeric type, and a credential-hygiene gap that .gitignore alone did not close - generalize to any small scientific-software project built by a domain expert without formal software-engineering training. Both the system and the lessons from building it are reported here; two follow-on papers cover the validated characterization pipelines (Stage 2) and the retrieval-augmented synthesis advisor and CALPHAD thermodynamics module (Stage 3) built on this foundation.

items.title: Methods for Deriving Nonlinear Kinetic Equations from the Dynamics of Quantum Systems
items.summary: The article outlines key topics related to deriving kinetic equations and, in general, to the relationship between the evolution equations governing quantum many-particle systems. The main issues being considered are the mathematical origin of quantum kinetic equations, novel methods for deriving kinetic equations from hierarchies of evolution equations for quantum systems, specifically focusing on kinetics within the framework of the evolution of observables, and the generalization of the quantum kinetic equation specified by non-separable initial states.

items.title: Tunable flat bands from a parent chiral Hamiltonian
authors: Jun-Hyung Bae, Alexei Andreanov, Saurabh Maiti
items.summary: Systems with flat bands are interesting as they potentially host many exotic quantum phenomena that would be hard to observe in usual systems with dispersive bands. Multiple approaches were developed to construct flat band systems, with most of them requiring fine-tuning and/or solving a challenging inverse-eigenvalue problem. In this article we work with an idea that uses a parent bipartite system to generate a family of flat bands by means of Hilbert space projections. This method is largely free from fine-tuning constraints and allows us to identify conditions for a Hamiltonian to guarantee flat bands at desired energies, with desired degree of degeneracy. We also show that one can control the touching points of the flat band with dispersive bands at any desirable point in the Brillouin zone. In the process, we identify perturbations that preserve the flat bands or split them controllably. This approach provides easy tunability in designing flat band systems with desired properties.

items.title: CRAFT-{\epsilon}: A Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for the Static Relative Permittivity of Pure Organic Liquids
items.summary: The static relative permittivity is an important property in thermodynamic modeling, electrochemistry, and solvent design, but predicting it directly from molecular structure remains challenging because both electronic polarization and molecular dipole orientation contribute to the measured response. Here, we introduce CRAFT-{\epsilon} (Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for {\epsilon}), a conformer-resolved molecular descriptor model for predicting the static relative permittivity of neutral pure liquids. Conformer free energies, molecular dipoles, and atom-resolved polarizabilities are obtained from a GFN2-xTB/ALPB 10 workflow. The molecular dipole is decomposed into chemically defined polar-fragment vectors, allowing fitted corrections to retain both the magnitude and relative orientation of local dipolar contributions. Electronic and orientational polarization are combined with a group-contribution molar volume in the Onsager-Kirkwood-Fr\"ohlich relation. A staged parameterization with 41 parameters is applied to nonpolar, polar, and hydrogen-bonding compounds. For 1393 liquids with permittivities between 1.5 and 183, CRAFT-{\epsilon} reaches a five-fold cross-validated average absolute deviation of 2.40 ({R^2} = 0.93). Conformational averaging 15 is essential for liquids with several polar groups. Compared with an established fragment-based model with 139 parameters, it reaches a similar cross-validated RMSE (3.65 versus 3.41) with about a quarter of the parameters and applies to every liquid of the dataset. The resulting framework provides a computationally inexpensive route from molecular structure to liquid dielectric response and forms a basis for later application to solvent mixtures and electrolyte systems.

items.title: Higher-Order Flatband-Touching Points Mediate Unconventional Bulk-Boundary Correspondence
authors: Limin Song, Jianqi Xiong, Liqin Tang, Daohong Song, Zhigang Chen
items.summary: The bulk-boundary correspondence establishes a fundamental connection between bulk band topology and the emergence of boundary states, underpinning topological phenomena across electronic, acoustic, photonic, and many other wave systems. A broad class of singular flatband systems, however, exhibits an unconventional form of bulk-boundary correspondence, in which robust boundary modes (RBMs) originate from flatband-touching points (FBTPs) and the real-space topology associated with incomplete sets of compact localized states (CLSs), rather than conventional momentum-space bulk topological invariants. To date, experimental studies of such boundary modes have been limited to systems hosting lower-order FBTPs. Here, we experimentally demonstrate unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence in a photonic cross-bedded Kagome-like lattice featuring a higher-order FBTP formed by the touching of two degenerate flatbands and a dispersive band. Using continuous-wave laser writing, we observe shape-preserving propagation of both bulk CLSs and boundary RBMs. Remarkably, unlike previously reported flatband systems, the RBMs retain their boundary localization under input-field perturbations involving both singular and nonsingular CLSs, revealing an unconventional boundary response associated with the higher-order FBTP in this lattice. Our results establish the Kagome-like lattice as a new platform for exploring flatband physics and unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence, with potential applications in wave localization, flatband lasers, and other emerging topological photonic devices.

items.title: Binder migration across film consolidation and pore emptying in electrode drying: a continuous model validated against drying-rate, thickness, and schedule experiments
authors: Younghwan Joo, Sanghyun Oh, Sung-il Kim
items.summary: Drying battery electrodes faster saves energy but drives dissolved binder toward the film surface, depleting the current-collector interface and weakening adhesion. Models of this migration stop convecting the binder when film consolidation ends, and models of the subsequent pore emptying omit the binder or start from an assumed binder field, so no simulation has followed binder convection through both stages that a drying schedule acts on. This study presents a continuous simulation of the dissolved binder field across both stages, driven by the published drying rates and completed by effective descriptions of the two questions the base transport physics leaves open: where the liquid of the consolidating film carries the binder, and when the binder stops moving as the pores empty. With a single parameter set, the simulation reproduces three types of published measurements: the change of the surface-to-interface binder ratio with drying rate over a factor of 5.6 and the surface and interface binder levels of films six times thicker; concentration profiles through the film interior; and the response of the interface binder to the time at which the drying rate is switched mid-process. Applied without further adjustment to a published three-stage schedule, the model reproduces the shortened drying and the full interface recovery when the rate is lowered early, and shows that its final high-rate stage begins after the binder has stopped. Combined with a coater-scale process model, the model can be used to identify operating points for electrode production that improve energy efficiency and product quality together.

items.title: Boundary exceptional point driven chiral switch of topological edge states
items.summary: We theoretically investigate the interplay of topology and localized non-Hermiticity in a finite Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain characterized by non-Hermitian potentials at its boundaries. By tuning the boundary gain and loss parameters, we exploit the finite-size hybridization of two mid-gap topological edge states to analytically derive the exact coordinates of boundary-induced exceptional points (EPs), $\Gamma_{\rm EP}=\pm i v^{N}/w^{N-1}$, at which these states undergo coalescence. We demonstrate that dynamically encircling these boundary EPs facilitates a robust, chiral edge state-transfer protocol. Depending on the orientation of the encircling loop, this protocol allows a topological edge state localized at one boundary to be either transferred to the opposite edge with perfect fidelity or returned to its starting position through a double switching process. Importantly, since the non-Hermiticity remains strictly confined to the boundaries, this chiral transport occurs without affecting the energy spectrum of the bulk bands. These results establish a minimal framework for a large-scale topological chiral switch that is experimentally verifiable and capable of being controlled through boundary non-Hermitian driving.

items.title: Compositional neural networks for multimodal X-ray and neutron scattering inversion
authors: Valentin Munteanu, Alexander Hinderhofer, Dmitry Lapkin, Vladimir Starostin, Frank Schreiber
items.summary: X-ray and neutron scattering are indispensable for structural characterization across condensed-matter physics and materials science. Yet, because scattering experiments generally record intensities without phase information, distinct structures can yield similar scattering patterns, rendering the corresponding inverse problems non-unique. This ambiguity can be reduced by combining complementary measurements, but their integration into machine-learning frameworks remains challenging. Here we introduce a modular framework for probabilistic multi-measurement analysis based on prior-amortized flow matching. Single-observation posterior estimators are trained separately for individual observation types or physical probes and combined only at inference time through a compositional sampler. This late fusion approach allows pretrained single-observation models to be reused without dedicated joint retraining. As a case in point, we consider reflectometry, which provides depth-resolved, nanometer-scale information about thin films and interfaces. Our single-observation demonstrations span X-ray, time-of-flight neutron and polarized neutron reflectometry. In separate co-refinement studies, task-matched estimators enable homogeneous composition across multiple neutron contrasts and heterogeneous multimodal composition of X-ray and neutron measurements. Together, these results establish compositional flow matching as a modular approach to uncertainty-aware inversion and co-refinement, with potential applicability to other scattering problems in which multiple observations constrain a common physical structure while retaining measurement-specific parameters.

items.title: Phase Transitions in Learning Driven by Extremal Data
items.summary: We study an extremal regression problem, an example of multiple instance learning (MIL), where the predictors are given as multisets, called bags. The bag elements (called instances) possess hidden labels which are pooled to produce an observed bag-level label. Max pooling is common in MIL applications, but gives rise to vanishing gradients. To handle this, modern MIL pipelines approximate the max with a softmax, treating the sharpness as a learnable parameter, denoted $\lambda$. When the max pooling model is the true data generating process, learning will be successful when $\lambda$ is increased during gradient descent, thereby driving the dynamics into regions of parameter space with vanishing gradients. To understand the conditions under which gradient descent breaks down, we study a minimal model and derive a low dimensional projection of the gradient flow in the joint limit of large bags $n$ and high dimension $d$ with $\alpha=\ln n/d$ fixed. The flow has two distinct phase transitions: an intrinsic freezing transition related to the random energy model of disordered systems, and a retrieval transition occurring in modern Hopfield networks. Numerical simulation confirms both the phase diagram and the convergence of the finite-size training gradient to its predicted asymptotic form.

items.title: Quantum-Enhanced Matterwave Interferometry in a Ring Waveguide
items.summary: We propose a quantum-enhanced matter-wave interferometry protocol based on fractional-revival dynamics of a Bose-Einstein condensate in a ring, combined with a controlled interaction quench. Using the Truncated Wigner Approximation, we show that nonlinear evolution to the quarter revival generates modest spin squeezing of $-2.03\pm0.28\;$dB, which subsequently degrades under further nonlinear evolution. In contrast, starting from a non-interacting condensate, a controlled interaction quench applied after the initial quarter-revival beam-splitter operation generates substantially stronger spin squeezing of $-14.57\pm0.27\;$dB. We further show that phase control at $t=3T_r/8$ rotates the squeezed quadrature onto the phase-sensitive direction $\hat{J}_y$, producing a phase-squeezed state at $t=T_r/2$. The subsequent quarter-revival evolution converts this phase-squeezed state into a number-squeezed state, enabling population-difference readout. The resulting sequence provides a route to quantum-enhanced interferometry using the intrinsic fractional-revival dynamics of a ring together with controlled interaction and phase operations.

items.title: Geometrization of continuum mechanics and nonequilibrium thermodynamics: Heat conduction
items.summary: We propose a geometric formulation of non-equilibrium heat conduction. It combines the variational (Hamiltonian) structure of symmetric hyperbolic thermodynamically compatible (SHTC) equations with the exterior calculus of differential forms. The central object is the thermal impulse one-form on the four-dimensional matter-time manifold. Its time component is the temperature, and for reversible (ballistic) heat transport it is the exact differential of a scalar potential (i.e. it is holonomic). Non-equilibrium effects are described by a second one-form, the small-scale thermal impulse, which is not required to be exact. Its time component is a fluctuating temperature, and its exterior derivative, the four-thermal vorticity, satisfies a Bianchi-type kinematic identity. The variational principle together with this identity yields a non-equilibrium two-temperature model. Its field equations have the same structure as Maxwell's equations in a medium, with the thermal impulse field, the thermal vorticity field and a thermal Poynting vector contributing to the heat flux. Dissipation is introduced through relaxation terms that conserve the total energy and produce entropy. A formal asymptotic analysis shows that, in the relaxation limit, the model reduces to a Guyer-Krumhansl-type heat conduction with independent transverse and longitudinal length scales. The transverse nonlocal term comes from the spatial non-holonomy of the small-scale thermal impulse, while the longitudinal term comes from its non-holonomy in time, i.e. from the relaxation of the fluctuating temperature. We also discuss the gauge-theoretic interpretation of the model. Its kinematics is that of an abelian gauge theory, while the local gauge symmetry is explicitly broken by the existence of two temperatures. Finally, we discuss the consequences of the geometric structure for structure-preserving numerical methods.

items.title: Choosing Spatial Resolution in the Residence-Time Approach to Local Diffusivity
authors: Michael von Domaros, Rinto Thomas, Praveen Ranganath Prabhakar
items.summary: Estimating position-dependent diffusivity with the residence-time approach (RTA) requires choosing an interval width that resolves spatial variation while probing time scales compatible with a local diffusion model. We develop a selection criterion that combines bulk diffusivity convergence with local model agreement measured by the Kullback-Leibler divergence between observed and predicted first-exit-time distributions, and assess global model agreement through independent propagator analysis against unbiased molecular dynamics. Applications to water in a fluid phospholipid bilayer and three permeants in a model skin lipid barrier show that local agreement alone does not ensure global fidelity: in the skin barrier, narrow intervals minimize exit-time mismatch but predict excessive spreading, whereas requiring bulk convergence selects wider intervals with better longer-time predictions. In propagator tests, RTA profiles at the selected interval widths outperform velocity-autocorrelation-based profiles and generally improve agreement relative to position-autocorrelation-based profiles in the skin barrier, while phospholipid-bilayer rankings depend on lag time and discrepancy metric; both autocorrelation methods use harmonically restrained simulations.

items.title: Hierarchical Response Theory of Electronegativity from Atomic Mean Inner Potential
items.summary: Electronegativity, introduced by Pauling nearly a century ago, remains chemistry's most widely used yet conceptually ambiguous quantity: is it a fixed atomic constant, or does it depend on chemical environment? We resolve this debate by recasting electronegativity as a continuous response function rooted in the Atomic Mean Inner Potential (AMIP), a quantum-mechanical observable accessible through first-principles calculation and, ultimately, electron holography. Expanding the AMIP with respect to fractional electron removal defines a hierarchy of physically distinct coefficients: the static electronegativity $\chi_0$, the Electrostatic Rigidity $\mathcal{R}$---whose sign indicates whether an atom hardens or softens upon oxidation---and the Electrostatic Anharmonic Modulus $\mathcal{A}$. A logarithmic-derivative decomposition links these coefficients to two competing microscopic channels, electronic screening loss and geometric volume collapse, whose balance governs the response of all 102 elements. This competition produces a systematic dichotomy between softening main-group elements and hardening d-block elements, two scaling laws within the transition series (closed-shell stiffening and principal quantum softening), and two anomalies: a pronounced exchange-driven effect at half-filled d$^{5}$ configurations and a near-perfect cancellation in Ce. It also resolves the long-standing Cs--Fr controversy, identifying Fr as a critical element whose near-boundary response is amplified fivefold by relativistic contraction of the 7s orbital. The framework reproduces the classical Allen, Pauling, and Mulliken scales as well as Lewis acidity trends, and makes three falsifiable experimental predictions. It transforms electronegativity from a lookup-table number into a predictive, hierarchically structured quantum descriptor.

items.title: Reducing strain fluctuations in quantum dot devices by gate-layer stacking
authors: Collin C. D. Frink, Talise Oh, E. S. Joseph, Merritt P. Losert, E. R. MacQuarrie, Benjamin D. Woods, M. A. Eriksson, Mark Friesen
items.summary: Nanofabricated metal gate electrodes are commonly used to confine and control electrons in electrostatically defined quantum dots. However, these same gates impart strain-induced potential fluctuations that can potentially impair device functionality. Here we investigate strain fluctuations in Si/SiGe heterostructures, caused by (i) lattice mismatch, (ii) materials-dependent thermal contraction, and (iii) depositional stress in the metal gates.By simulating gate geometries, ranging from simple to realistically complicated, we identify two opposing effects in overlapping gate structures: (a) gate-driven behavior arising from isolated gates vs (b) oxide-driven behavior arising from the thin oxides separating the gates in an overlapping geometry. These limiting behaviors induce strains of opposite sign, pointing towards the possibility of suppressing strain fluctuations through careful design. Here, we demonstrate in numerical models, a nearly total suppression of short-range strain fluctuation through device optimization. These results suggest that strain fluctuations should not pose an insurmountable challenge to qubit uniformity, provided that oxide and overlapping gate thicknesses can be tuned.

items.title: Comment on "InAs-Al hybrid devices passing the topological gap protocol", Microsoft Quantum, Phys. Rev. B 107, 245423 (2023)
items.summary: The topological gap protocol (TGP) is presented as "a series of stringent experimental tests" for the presence of topological superconductivity and associated Majorana zero modes. Here, we show that the TGP, "passed" by Microsoft Quantum [PRB 107, 245423 (2023)], lacks a consistent definition of "gap" or "topological", and even utilises different code when applied to theoretical simulations compared to experimental data. Furthermore, the outcome of the TGP is sensitive to the choice of magnetic field range, bias voltage range, data resolution, and cutter voltage pair (junction transparency) -- data parameters that, in PRB 107, 245423 (2023), vary significantly, even for measurements of the same device. As a result, the core claims of PRB 107, 245423 (2023) are based on unexplained measurement choices and inconsistent definitions. In particular, this means the claim by Microsoft Quantum in PRB 107, 245423 (2023) that their devices have a "high probability of being in the topological phase" is not reliable and should be revisited. In light of this, subsequent studies that are based on tuning up devices via the TGP should also be revisited.

items.title: Pseudomagnetic focusing of valley-polarized beams in strained graphene
authors: Alina Mre\'nca-Kolasi\'nska, Christophe De Beule, Jia-Tong Shi, Aitor Garcia-Ruiz, Denis Kochan, Klaus Richter, Ming-Hao Liu
items.summary: In addition to spin, the low-energy charge carriers in graphene have two inequivalent valley flavors K and K' related by time-reversal symmetry, which can potentially serve as carriers for additional information. One promising route of controlling the valley degree of freedom relies on strain-induced pseudomagnetic fields, which couple with opposite signs to the two valleys. In this work, we theoretically investigate quantum transport in strained graphene devices that host tailored pseudomagnetic field profiles for valley manipulation. We focus on experimentally feasible geometries and propose transverse pseudomagnetic focusing in a bent graphene ribbon as an efficient method for generating valley-polarized currents, even in presence of disorder. Our work highlights pseudomagneto-transport in graphene as a viable tool for valleytronic applications.

items.title: Fast and Sensitive Readout of a Semiconductor Quantum Dot Using an In-Situ Microwave Resonator with Enhanced Gate Lever Arm
items.summary: We report an experimental study of a Si/SiGe double quantum dot (DQD) directly coupled to a niobium superconducting coplanar stripline (CPS) microwave resonator. This hybrid architecture enables high-bandwidth dispersive readout suitable for real-time feedback and error-correction protocols. Fast and sensitive readout is achieved primarily by optimizing the DQD gate lever arm, guided by MaSQE quantum dot simulations, which enhances the dispersive signal without requiring high-impedance resonators. We demonstrate a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of unity with an integration time of 34.54 nanoseconds, corresponding to a system bandwidth of 14.48 MHz and a charge sensitivity of 0.000186 e per square root hertz. Analysis of the voltage power spectral density (PSD) of the in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) baseband signals characterizes the system's readout noise, with the PSD's dependence on integration time providing insight into distinct physical regimes.

items.title: Resonating-valence-bond superconductor from small Fermi surface in twisted bilayer graphene
items.summary: Understanding the mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is a central challenge in correlated moir\'e materials. The most intriguing question is about the nature of the normal state: is the Cooper pair formed from small Fermi surface or large Fermi surface? Here, we propose a unified theoretical framework describing a symmetric pseudogap metal with small hole pockets, dubbed the second Fermi liquid (sFL), which is topologically distinct from the conventional Fermi liquid. Our theory shows that superconductivity in TBG emerges from the sFL phase, with local moment pairing transferred to mobile carriers, giving rise to a smaller nodal superconducting gap on the small hole pockets. This framework simultaneously explains the pseudogap metal above the transition temperature and the two-gap nematic superconductivity below it, providing a comprehensive understanding of correlated physics in TBG.

items.title: Josephson Oscillation and Nonlinear Self-Trapping in Quasi-one-dimensional Quantum Liquid
authors: Shivam Singh,  Ibrar, Suhail Rashid, Ayan Khan
items.summary: In this article, we study the two-mode method to analyze the Josephson oscillation for a trapped binary Bose-Einstein condensate while taking into account the beyond mean-field and three body interactions. For this purpose, we use the archetypal model of double well potential and study the Josephson oscillation and self-trapping phases in quasi-one dimension. Additionally, our analysis provides quantitative discussion on the effect of asymmetry and dimension. We further corroborate our findings with Bogoliubov quasi-particle method and notice the existence of roton-like mode.
